propositions: Blue-green cutover swaps the nginx /mcp upstream to a new container immediately, orphaning all client sessions with Mcp-Session-Id because session state is per-container and the old container is no longer routed to

Clients holding an Mcp-Session-Id receive 404 Session expired when their next request routes to a container that never created that session, surfaced as opaque rmcp::transport::worker errors rather than actionable reconnect signals

The retire path keeps the old container alive with docker stop --time 1260 (21 minutes) but switches the upstream FIRST, so no request reaches the retiring container to drain sticky sessions, making the graceful-drain logs describe protection that cannot apply

Stateless mode (stateless_http=True in FastMCP and mcp.streamable_http_app) makes session orphaning structurally impossible because no per-container session state exists to lose during blue-green cutover

Live validation across three simulated cutovers confirms that after enabling stateless mode, a single MCP client session survived all three upstream swaps without Session expired errors or transport failures, with all tool calls returning successfully
